thread:
oncall-bot: Paging: High 95th latency observed for runtime-prod in us-west-2. Impacting ~18% of requests. Alert ID: RUNTIME-PLG-4312 :rotating_light:

liz-oncall: Saw the alert, joining. Can someone confirm if this correlates with the rollout from this morning?

sam-eng: yes, we rolled the 2026-03 runtime build at 08:05 with the new batching kernel selector (gradual canary). Canary traffic at ~5% started ~08:10.

maria-sre: metrics look like increased tail latency and a surge in kernel-fallback count on canary shard group. KV cache miss rate also jumped. Dumping traces now.

dave-runtime: confirming kernel fallback trips on nodes running the new selector. Error logs show: `kernel_select: fallback_to_generic: reason=unaligned_smem` repeated.

liz-oncall: @sam-eng please flip the feature flag for the selector on canary to off, then hold. We need to stop further rollouts.

sam-eng: flipping flag now: `./ffctl set runtime_selector_enabled=false --scope=canary`

oncall-bot: Feature flag change detected: runtime_selector_enabled=false by sam-eng. Traffic rollouts paused.

alex-product: @liz-oncall any estimated customer impact? We're getting pings from a small set of customers about slow responses.

maria-sre: preliminary CS routing shows ~60 support tickets with slow-generation complaints in the last 20m. Most are mid-size customers using streaming chat. Not yet widespread but rising.

dave-runtime: after flag flip, kernel-fallback counts dropping but MQ backlog rising on the canary pool — batching logic isn't reclaiming capacity quickly. Looks like microbatch windows are stuck at 80ms.

liz-oncall: ok, that's dangerous — we avoid increasing latency by piling up backlog. @sam-eng can you trigger a canary rollback to previous runtime build and drain the canary pool?

sam-eng: scheduling rollback to build 2026-02. Command: `deployctl rollback --cluster runtime-canary --to 2026-02`

oncall-bot: Deploy rollback started by sam-eng. Watch: https://releases/redwood/rollback/3187654321

maria-sre: I'm switching alert to P1 and paging oncall ops team. Please keep a live log of actions and customer-facing notes.

cs-bot: Notifying top 10 affected customers with templated message: "We're investigating latency issues affecting some requests in US-WEST. We're rolling back a recent runtime change and will provide updates."

sam-eng: rollback finished and canary drained. Verified canary nodes back on 2026-02; kernel-fallback rates returned to baseline.

dave-runtime: batch window reset after drain, queues cleared. Latency 95th trending back to normal. Still watching for any stragglers.

liz-oncall: Good. Maria — can you run a quick RCA triage doc (short) and list immediate mitigations to prevent auto-rollout until we patch selector logic? Also add a guard to block `unaligned_smem` cases.

maria-sre: on it. I'll create postmortem stub and add action items: patch selector alignment check, increase canary observability for kernel fallback, add a pre-rollout synthetic load test for microbatch behavior.

alex-product: We'll prepare a brief customer update for impacted accounts once RCA draft ready. Keep CS on the loop.

oncall-bot: Incident resolved: latency restored to baseline and rollback completed. Close after 2h of stable metrics.

liz-oncall: staying on watch for 1 hour for any reoccurrence. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sam-eng: Adding a temporary rollout block: `ffctl block rollout --tag runtime-selector --until 2026-04-01`

maria-sre: Logged follow-ups in the incident tracker: INC-2026-4312. Will attach traces and the dump of `kernel_select` logs.

cs-bot: CS update sent to affected accounts. Template included workaround: reduce sustained concurrent message volume if possible.

liz-oncall: Closing communication loop: no customer escalations beyond initial reports. Good job on the quick rollback.

sam-eng: retrospective: root cause: selector assumed 64-byte aligned shared memory layouts; newer kernels in the canary nodes changed padding. Fix will add explicit alignment checks and fallback to safe path only after batch size/latency threshold.

maria-sre: I'll schedule a focused dry-run in staging that simulates mixed kernel versions and run microbatch pressure tests before we attempt another rollout.

liz-oncall: End of thread — will convert to PM ticket and assign owners. Thanks team.
